SENDERS (`transcriptLayout(input)`, every mirror replays `cases` comparing the WHOLE expected array): an item is `message` (a card-less message row, a child's report, a pending input), `trace` (a tool, thought or subagent line of the agent's work, the raw session view's feed) or `full` (every card: a `Workflow` call's Work card (#EXP-1750), question, plan, to-do, suggestions, session card, picture, surface, event line, divider, locked pill; full width, never grouped). Any other agent message = the chat's OWN agent: `chat.agentId` set = `kind agent` (id = agentId, name = agents[agentId].name, else `chat.title`), else `kind session` (id = `chat.sessionId`, name = `chat.title`; owner's answer: in a plain session the agent's bubbles wear the session title + the session avatar); `link` null. A `user` message carrying an `authorSessionId` of another known session (a session posting as its starter) is cross-session too. ORIGIN (one rule ×4, data first): `chat.originSessionId` = the session that STARTED the viewed one, from the synced rows (its `parentId`, else the agent conversation that started its root: session-chat.json `origin`), never from prompt text; `chat.fromStart` = the items begin at the conversation's very first message (no `Load earlier` above them). When both hold, the FIRST INPUT (a `message` item with `authorKind` `user`, or one carrying a known cross-session `authorSessionId`) reads as sent by the origin whoever the row names (in the raw session feed that first prompt is a typed turn), unless it carries that known cross-session `authorSessionId` itself (in a chat the prompt row names its sender, data wins); either way no later row takes the origin. The agent's own output is NEVER re-attributed: agent rows before the first input stay the chat's own. Parsing the prompt text (`inputCases`) is only the fallback for a session input the feed carries no author for. A `trace` item belongs to the chat's OWN agent sender (it never shows a name). An unknown `authorSessionId` falls back to the rule without it. GROUPING: consecutive non-full items with the same sender (kind + id + link; `own` = one sender) form one group; `avatar` = true on a group's FIRST item (#FEED-239: own groups too, the avatar on the right; #EXP-1854: the own TAIL (message-delivery.json: the no-feed placeholder's sent inputs, the unconsumed rows, the outbox) is own items after the transcript's last, so when no transcript row carries the own group's avatar its first bubble does, beside its tail); `name` = true on a group's first `message` item when it is not own; `tail` = true on a group's first `message` item, own or not (#EXP-1876, Danny's option A: THE bubble's tail sits on the group's FIRST bubble only, at its TOP corner beside the avatar, pointing LEFT for anyone else (genUI MessageBubble `tail: start`) and RIGHT for the viewer's own (`tail: end`); every follow-on bubble has none; the tail = 6 px out × 9 px down, a sharp top edge continuing the bubble's top, a straight hypotenuse back into the side, a ~2 px rounded tip, that corner's radius 0, the same fill + hairline as the bubble drawn as ONE outline, inside the `layout.avatarGap`: no layout change); `gap` (the space above the row) = 0 on the first item, `layout.gapInGroup` inside a group, else `layout.gapBetween`. The text of a session input on the device (`inputCases`, `crossSessionInput(text)`): the raw session view gets a parent's or child's message as a prompt line `Report from <name> (session <id>, ended): <summary>` or `Message from <name> (session <id>): <body>` (desktop `coding::pickup::input_text`); it parses to `{kind: report|message, name, sessionId, body}` (the pattern `^(Report|Message) from (.+?) \(session ([^,)\s]+)(, ended)?\): ([\s\S]*)$`, the name the shortest prefix that matches) and draws as that session's cross-session bubble (`body` the bubble's text); `<name>` = the member's name off the synced users, else `copy.formerMember`; a private conversation and every other chat keep the bare body; a system input keeps its `[<key>] ` tag and a pressed view's `[action]` line its own form); a group chat's brief has NO Request (session-brief.json: the server composes it without the first message and its claim consumes none), so the chat's FIRST message is delivered as an input like every later one and is worded too, so the agent knows who wrote it; #EXP-2119: a card's ANSWER is a person's input too: the server stamps the clear `answeredBy` (the member's user id; absent when a session answered) on an answered question / plan card, and the device delivers the answer's text (plan-card.json `answerText`) worded with that member exactly like their message; `feedInput` reads it as `{kind: member, name, userId, body}` (`feedInputCases`) and the raw session feed draws it as a `message` whose `authorKind` is `user` and `authorId` that member (the viewer's own = their own bubble right; anyone else's left under their avatar and name, `members[userId]` else the line's `name`), its bubble holding the `body` alone. A system input is THE inline MARKER ×4 (the feed's `Context compacted` row: a centred muted label between two hairlines, full width, never grouped): `feedInput(text)` (`feedInputCases`) reads a feed input as `{kind: marker, key, label}` when the device tagged it (`coding::pickup::input_text` leads a message carrying an `event` card with `[<key>] `: `schedule` = a schedule firing (`trigger_fired` without a name), `event` = an event firing or any other event, `pr_opened`, `pr_merged`, `pr_merge`, `pr_checks`, `session` = a session status line (`session_*`); the key must be one of `copy.markers`, label = `copy.markers[key]`), or, untagged (an older device), its body leads with the server's own firing text (`Schedule `…`` up to ` fired` = `schedule`; ``Event `<name>` (from `` = `event`); else `{kind: relay, …crossSessionInput}` for a cross-session input, else null (a person's prompt). A MARKER IS DRAWN ONLY ABOVE A REPLY (`markersShown(kinds)`, `markerCases`: kinds per feed row `marker` | `input` | `reply` (agent prose with text) | `other` (work, cards); a `marker` shows when a `reply` follows it before the next `input` or `marker`, every other row shows): a fire or event the agent answered silently draws nothing. A hidden marker is no transcript item at all (it never breaks a group). An agent turn whose text is blank draws nothing (no empty bubble). #EXP-1873 (Danny, 2026-11-15: "it's not quiet at all. it should be one line only.") A QUIET CHECK-IN IS ONE LINE ×4 (`feedRows(kinds)`, `checkInCases`; it wraps `markersShown`, every platform's main feed calls it instead): kinds per feed row `schedule` (a `schedule` marker: a schedule firing = a check-in) | `marker` (every other marker: an event, a PR or session line; event triggers do NOT count, an unanswered one stays hidden and its quiet turn keeps its own `Ended turn quietly`) | `input` | `reply` | `quiet` (the `session_self_quiet` notice row) | `blank` (an agent turn with blank text: never drawn) | `other` (work, cards, any shown tool line). A schedule row's TURN = the rows after it up to the next `schedule`, `marker` or `input` (or the end). It is a QUIET CHECK-IN when its turn has a `quiet` row and no `reply` or `other` row (Danny, 2026-11-16: nothing an agent says is ever hidden; a message written AFTER the quiet call, e.g. the CLI's forced `No change since my last update.`, makes it a normal turn: today's `Schedule` marker + the bubble, and it starts a new run). A quiet check-in draws ONE inline marker on the schedule row (THE `Context compacted` marker) and nothing else of its turn. CONSECUTIVE quiet check-ins (no drawn row between them; hidden rows never separate) collapse into ONE line on the LAST one's row, the earlier ones hidden. Per row the result is `false` (not drawn), `true` (drawn as itself, today's rule) or a number n (the check-in line covering n check-ins). Its label `checkInLabel(count, time)` (`checkInLabelCases`): count 1 = `copy.checkIn`, else `copy.checkIns` with `{count}`; a known time (the LAST check-in's firing, the schedule row's `at`, `HH:mm`) appends `copy.checkInTimeSeparator` + the time. A check-in that answered (a message before or after quiet, a card, a tool line) keeps today's rendering. The chat-transcript specimen ×4 draws `checkInSpecimen` (an agent chat's feed: kind, `HH:mm`, text) through `feedRows`: a run of quiet check-ins, one that answered (THE marker above the agent's bubble) and a second run; the answer is a real agent bubble (owner 2026-11-16): `checkInSpecimenAgent`'s avatar (THE agent avatar, its icon in its colour) left of it, its name inside, and the tail (the group's first bubble).

blank.$comment: #FEED-256 / #FEED-254 BLANK TEXT ×5 (`isBlankText(text)`, `blankCases`; web, desktop, iOS, Android and the driver (eagent `blank::is_blank_text`) replay it): a text is BLANK when every character in it is one of `codePoints` (hex Unicode scalars: the Unicode White_Space set plus the invisible format characters: soft hyphen, Mongolian vowel separator, zero-width space, zero-width non-joiner, zero-width joiner, LRM, RLM, word joiner, BOM); the empty text is blank. Never a platform's own trim (JS `trim` keeps U+200B, Rust/Swift/Kotlin differ on U+FEFF and U+00A0). THE DRIVER: a turn whose final text is blank posts no reply (nothing stored, nothing relayed to the person, a parent or a managing agent); the server treats a blank card-less reply as no message too. EVERY CLIENT: a stored card-less message with a blank body draws nothing (no bubble, no transcript item, it never breaks a group), a feed narration with blank text is the `blank` role, and so is a feed input that `feedInput` reads as a relay whose `body` is blank (#FEED-254: `Message from <name> (session <id>): ` followed by nothing) (`checkInCases`: a blank message after quiet keeps the check-in quiet). #FEED-255 ENTITIES: a text is blank too when its only other content is character references that DECODE to one of `codePoints`, exactly the ones genUI's markdown decodes (an invisible body drew a tall empty bubble): a decimal `&#<1-7 digits>;`, a hex `&#x<1-6 hex digits>;` (`x` or `X`) or the named ` `; a reference to any other code point, a malformed one (no `;`, too many digits, `�`, past U+10FFFF) or any other named entity (`&`) is visible text.
